programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.sub-title: The Great American Songbook with Samara Joy
programme.desc: Andi Oliver presents a BBC Proms concert in which American jazz singer Samara Joy and her octet join the BBC Concert Orchestra and conductor Miho Hazama to perform classic songs and musical standards at the Royal Albert Hall. Fresh from another double win at this year's Grammys, Joy makes her much-anticipated Proms debut, introducing audiences to her electric combination of youthful energy and old-soul musical style with classic songs and unique twists on instrumental classics from across jazz and its fringes, from bossa nova to the Great American Songbook. She salutes figures including Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald, Duke Ellington, Billie Holiday, Charles Mingus and Oscar Peterson. Nacio Herb Brown: You Stepped out of a Dream. Hoagy Carmichael: Stardust Davis, Ramirez and Sherman: Loverman (Oh Where Can You Be). Erroll Garner: Misty. Thelonius Monk: Worry Later (San Francisco Holiday). Billie Holiday and Max Waldron: Left Alone. Axel Stordahl and Paul Weston: Day by Day. Interval: Jazz singer and broadcaster Clare Teal joins Petroc to reflect on Samara Joy's Proms debut and to discuss the enduring fascination of the Great American Songbook. Betty Carter: Beware My Heart. Duke Ellington: I Got it Bad and That Ain't Good. Sun Ra, Samara Joy, Jae Mayo & Kendric McCallister: Peace of Mind/Dreams Come True. Samara Joy and Kendric Mccallister: Five Stages of Love (Love's Impression). Teddy Wilson and Harold Adamson: It's the Little Things that Mean So Much Monk: Ugly Beauty. Jobim: Chega de Saudade (No More Blues). Samara Joy (singer), Samara Joy Octet, BBC Concert Orchestra, conductor Miho Hazama

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes examines the progress of American art between 1929 and 1941, as the country struggled out of deep depression into an era of new prosperity. While Europe limped out of one war into another, the US presented a utopian vision of the future through its art and architecture until the veneer of isolationist naivety was destroyed by the bombing of Pearl Harbour

programme.title: This World
programme.sub-title: The Coffee Trail with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: In the second of two This World documentaries examining the stories behind the nation's favourite beverages, adventurer and broadcaster Simon Reeve looks at the production of coffee. He heads to Vietnam, which is the UK's biggest supplier, and travels to the remote central highlands where he meets some of the millions who grow, pick and pack the beans for instant coffee brands. The boom in the industry has made some people very rich, but Simon learns that the rapid success has come at a cost to both the locals and the environment

programme.title: London: A Tale of Two Cities with Dan Cruickshank

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: South Africa v Canada (Kick-off 8.00pm). Coverage of the opening round-of-32 match, which comes from Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA. After a mammoth group stage consisting of 72 games, only 16 of the 48 teams have been eliminated, with 32 nations taking part in the knockout stage for the first time in World Cup history. Co-hosts Canada finished second in Group B to progress to the knockout stages for the first time in their history, despite losing 2-1 to Switzerland in their final group match on Wednesday. South Africa pulled off a surprise 1-0 victory against South Korea in Group A to set up this meeting as they finished second behind Mexico to also secure World Cup knockout football for the first-ever time

programme.desc: Isa Guha presents coverage of day one of the third Grand Slam tournament of the year, held at the All England Club, featuring men's and ladies' first-round singles matches. Carlos Alcaraz began the defence of his title last year on Centre Court with a hard-fought 7-5, 6-7, 7-5, 2-6, 6-1 victory over Fabio Fognini. Over on Court No. 1, top women's seed Aryna Sabalenka claimed a 6-1, 7-5 victory over Carson Branstine, before João Fonseca also prevailed in straight sets against British hope Jacob Fearnley. However, there was success for a home favourite elsewhere, with Sonay Kartal triumphing 7-5, 2-6, 6-2 against 2017 French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v Japan (Kick-off 6.00pm). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Houston Stadium in the USA. Brazil finished top of Group C on goal difference ahead of Morocco after picking up seven points across their three group games. They will face a Japan side that finished second in Group F behind the Netherlands, after they drew 1-1 with Sweden who had to settle for third place. The Asian side were unbeaten across their three group games, winning once after hammering Tunisia 4-0 and drawing twice including a thrilling 2-2 draw against the Netherlands

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Germany v Group A/B/C/D/F third-placed team (Kick-off 9.30pm). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Boston Stadium in the USA. Germany thrashed Curaçao 7-1 and then came from behind to edge out Ivory Coast to secure their place as Group E winners. It might be expected for the third-placed qualifiers to struggle in this round, but the last two times the format allowed some of the teams finishing in third to reach the knockout stage were in the 24-team tournaments of 1990 and 1994, and on those occasions, Argentina and Italy respectively made it all the way to the final after progressing from outside the top two

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Netherlands v Morocco (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. The European side made it through to this stage after they finished top of Group F thanks to winning two and drawing one of their three matches. 5-1 and 3-1 victories over Sweden and Tunisia put them through after they drew 2-2 with Japan in their opening match of the tournament. Morocco finished second in Group C behind five-time winners Brazil on goal difference, and beat Haiti 4-2 in their final game to end their group campaign on seven points and progress to the knockout stages for the second successive time. These two sides have met just the once in a competitive match when they faced each other in a group match at the 1994 World Cup. Netherlands won that game 2-1 thanks to goals from Dennis Bergkamp and Bryan Roy

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Algeria v Austria (Kick-off 3.00am). Coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as both sides play their final group game. This is just the second meeting between these two teams, with the previous coming 44 years ago in the first group stage of the 1982 World Cup. That fixture saw Austria come away with a 2-0 victory, which helped them progress to the next stage of the tournament at the expense of the Algerians in controversial circumstances. Austria and West Germany knew that a 1-0 win for the Germans in the final group game between the nations would see both teams progress, and so they played out the match without serious attempts to score once the Germans took the lead. This game became known as the 'Disgrace of Gijon' and led to FIFA changing the rules for future tournaments, with all final group games being held simultaneously to avoid a reoccurrence. Both of these teams have three points going into this last game and whoever wins here will finish second in the group behind Argentina. Austria have the slight advantage though and will finish second here if they avoid defeat due to their superior goal difference

programme.desc: Colombia v Portugal (Kick-off 12.30am). All the action from both teams' third and final match in Group K, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. Perhaps surprisingly given both teams have made a number of appearances in this competition over the years, this is the first meeting between the nations. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: South Africa v Canada (Kick-off 8.00pm). Peter Collins presents coverage of the opening round-of-32 match, which comes from Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA. After a mammoth group stage consisting of 72 games, only 16 of the 48 teams have been eliminated, with 32 nations taking part in the knockout stage for the first time in World Cup history. Co-hosts Canada finished second in group B after losing 2-1 to Switzerland in their final group match on Wednesday to progress to the knock-out stages for the first time in their history. South Africa pulled off a surprise 1-0 victory against South Korea in group A to set up this meeting as they finished second in their group behind Mexico. With analysis from James McClean and Richie Sadlier

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Brazil v Japan (Kick-off 6.00pm). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Houston Stadium in the USA. Brazil finished top of Group C on goal difference ahead of Morocco after picking up seven points across their three group games. They will face a Japan side that finished second in Group F behind the Netherlands, after they drew 1-1 with Sweden who had to settle for third place. The Asian side were unbeaten across their three group games, winning once after hammering Tunisia 4-0 and drawing twice including a thrilling 2-2 draw against the Netherlands. Tony O'Donoghue presents, with analysis from Kevin Doyle

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.sub-title: Germany v Group A/B/C/D/F Third Place
programme.desc: Germany v Group A/B/C/D/F third-placed team (Kick-off 9.30pm). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Boston Stadium in the USA. Germany thrashed Curaçao 7-1 and then came from behind to edge out Ivory Coast to secure their place as Group E winners. It might be expected for the third-placed qualifiers to struggle in this round, but the last two times the format allowed some of the teams finishing in third to reach the knockout stage were in the 24-team tournaments of 1990 and 1994, and on those occasions, Argentina and Italy respectively made it all the way to the final after progressing from outside the top two. Germany thrashed Curaçao 7-1 and then came from behind to edge out Ivory Coast to secure their place as Group E winners. It might be expected for the third-placed qualifiers to struggle in this round, but the last two times the format allowed some of the teams finishing in third to reach the knockout stage were in the 24-team tournaments of 1990 and 1994, and on those occasions, Argentina and Italy respectively made it all the way to the final after progressing from outside the top two. programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are on the River Severn in Worcestershire to fish for zander, and enlist the help of local guide Tim Maslen to find the best spots. programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing

programme.title: Wild Brazil
programme.desc: The animal families face the formidable monsoon rains and the giant otter cubs must watch out for predatory jaguars and learn to swim before their river floods. The coatis have to eat as much as they can ahead of their habitat disappearing underwater, while the youngest capuchin monkey needs to master some clever survival skills. Stephen Mangan narrates
